blocks.etymology: From French précenteur, from Latin praecentor, from praecentus (“sung before”), from praecinō (“to sing before”) + -or (“agent suffix”), from prae- + canĕre (“to sing”).

blocks.etymology: Uncertain; perhaps an extended form of razz(le-dazzle). Compare pizzazz. Earliest citation from 1888, as razz-ma-taz.

thesaurus.definition: any exciting and complex play intended to confuse (dazzle) the opponent

vi_block: Sự quyến rũ và kích thích; sự phô trương ngông cuồng.

examples: He says he's late for the meeting because his daughter had an emergency at school, but I don't buy this razzmatazz.
wiktionary.gloss: Ambiguous or meaningless language.

examples: A few politicians are creating some razzmatazz about reinstating the draft.
wiktionary.gloss: Empty and tiresome speculation.

examples: Is he really the next big thing, or is all the media attention just a bunch of razzmatazz?
wiktionary.gloss: Something presenting itself in a fanciful and showy, often unrealistic manner, especially when intended to impress and confuse.

examples: When I finally got done dealing with all the razzmatazz of college registration, I decided to go out and have a drink.
wiktionary.gloss: A long and imposing series of mindless but necessary tasks.

blocks.etymology: Coined by the video game community and opponents of the lockout practice. The practice originated with and was devised by the video game industry and was later adopted by the film industry with the advent of DVDs.

wiktionary.gloss: The programming practice, code, or chip used to prevent the playing of imported media on a domestically marketed device.

blocks.etymology: From late Middle English seldom, alteration of earlier selden by analogy with adverbial datives such as whilom, from Old English seldan (“seldom”), from Proto-West Germanic *seldanā, from Proto-Germanic *seldanē. Cognate with Saterland Frisian säilden (“seldom”), West Frisian selden, komselden (“rare, seldom”), Dutch zelden, German selten, Danish sjælden, Norwegian Bokmål sjelden, Norwegian Nynorsk sjeldan, Swedish sällan, Faroese sjáldan, Icelandic sjaldan. More at seld and selly.

examples.en: We seldom eat dinner out during the week.
